1	import { LocalFileGroup } from './useFileTree'
2	import { SelectionItem } from './useSelection'
3	
4	// All ancestor group keys of a group key, from outermost to the key itself
5	// — e.g. "invoices/2026/jan" -> ["invoices", "invoices/2026", "invoices/2026/jan"]
6	// — derived from the '/'-joined key scheme GroupNode/FileList use to
7	// identify groups, without needing to walk the tree.
8	function keyChain(groupKey: string): string[] {
9	  const parts = groupKey.split('/')
10	  return parts.map((_, i) => parts.slice(0, i + 1).join('/'))
11	}
12	
13	// Maps every file's path to its immediate parent group's key, or null for a
14	// root-level file with no group to inherit from.
15	function fileParentKeys(tree: LocalFileGroup): Map<string, string | null> {
16	  const result = new Map<string, string | null>()
17	  const walk = (group: LocalFileGroup, groupKey: string | null) => {
18	    for (const file of group.files) result.set(file.path, groupKey)
19	    for (const sub of group.subgroups) {
20	      walk(sub, groupKey !== null ? `${groupKey}/${sub.name}` : sub.name)
21	    }
22	  }
23	  walk(tree, null)
24	  console.log(result)
25	  return result
26	}
27	
28	// Drops any selected item that's a descendant of another selected subfolder,
29	// so a batch assignment gives only the topmost selected item in each
30	// subtree its own assignment and leaves the rest to inherit it — instead of
31	// pinning every descendant with a redundant override that could later
32	// diverge from its ancestor's.
33	export function pruneSelectionForAssignment(tree: LocalFileGroup, items: SelectionItem[]): SelectionItem[] {
34	  const selectedGroupKeys = new Set(items.filter(i => i.type === 'group').map(i => i.key))
35	  const parentKeys = fileParentKeys(tree)
36	
37	  return items.filter(item => {
38	    if (item.type === 'group') {
39	      const ancestors = keyChain(item.key).slice(0, -1)
40	      return !ancestors.some(k => selectedGroupKeys.has(k))
41	    }
42	    const parentKey = parentKeys.get(item.path) ?? null
43	    if (parentKey === null) return true
44	    return !keyChain(parentKey).some(k => selectedGroupKeys.has(k))
45	  })
46	}

content.text:
Yes, worth merging — and it's more than tidiness. In `index.tsx:72`:

```ts
setPickerTargets(pruneSelectionForAssignment(tree, selection.items))
```

`pruneSelectionForAssignment` is typed to return `SelectionItem[]`, but it's being assigned into `pickerTargets`, which is `PickerTarget[]`. That only type-checks today because the two unions happen to be structurally identical — there's already an implicit assumption baked into the code that "a selected item" and "an assignment target" are the same thing. If either type drifted independently (e.g. someone added a field to one), this call site would break in a confusing way.

I'd keep the definition in `useSelection.ts` (it's the more foundational concept — selection exists independent of the picker) and have `useDriveAssignments.ts` import `SelectionItem` and use it directly as the parameter/return type wherever it currently says `PickerTarget`, dropping the separate type alias. `GroupNode.tsx` and `FileList.tsx` would just import `SelectionItem` instead.

Want me to make that change?

23	// an individual file (a file-level assignment overrides its group's).
24	// Resolving the *effective* assignment for a given group/file (own, else
25	// inherited from the nearest ancestor group, else none) is the caller's
26	// job, since only the caller knows the tree structure to walk.
27	export function useDriveAssignments(): DriveAssignmentsHandle {
28	  const [groupAssignments, setGroupAssignments] = useState<Map<string, DriveAssignment>>(new Map())
29	  const [fileOverrides, setFileOverrides] = useState<Map<string, DriveAssignment>>(new Map())
30	
31	  const setGroupAssignment = useCallback((groupKey: string, assignment: DriveAssignment) => {
32	    setGroupAssignments(prev => new Map(prev).set(groupKey, assignment))
33	  }, [])
34	
35	  const clearGroupAssignment = useCallback((groupKey: string) => {
36	    setGroupAssignments(prev => {
37	      const next = new Map(prev)
38	      next.delete(groupKey)
39	      return next
40	    })
41	  }, [])
42	
43	  const setFileOverride = useCallback((filePath: string, assignment: DriveAssignment) => {
44	    setFileOverrides(prev => new Map(prev).set(filePath, assignment))
45	  }, [])
46	
47	  const clearFileOverride = useCallback((filePath: string) => {
48	    setFileOverrides(prev => {
49	      const next = new Map(prev)
50	      next.delete(filePath)
51	      return next
52	    })
53	  }, [])
54	
55	  return { groupAssignments, fileOverrides, setGroupAssignment, clearGroupAssignment, setFileOverride, clearFileOverride }
56	}
57	
58	// Effective Drive assignment for every file in the tree: its own override,
59	// else the nearest ancestor group's assignment, else null. Mirrors the
60	// inheritance walk GroupNode/FileList do inline during render (same
61	// groupKey scheme: joined by '/', rooted at each top-level subgroup's own
62	// name), but usable outside a render tree — e.g. to check whether every
63	// file is ready to upload, or to build an upload job list.
64	export function resolveEffectiveAssignments(
65	  tree: LocalFileGroup,
66	  { groupAssignments, fileOverrides }: Pick<DriveAssignmentsHandle, 'groupAssignments' | 'fileOverrides'>
67	): Map<string, DriveAssignment | null> {
68	  const result = new Map<string, DriveAssignment | null>()
69	
70	  const walk = (group: LocalFileGroup, groupKey: string | null, inherited: DriveAssignment | null) => {
71	    const effective = (groupKey !== null ? groupAssignments.get(groupKey) : undefined) ?? inherited
72	    for (const file of group.files) {
73	      result.set(file.path, fileOverrides.get(file.path) ?? effective)
74	    }
75	    for (const sub of group.subgroups) {
76	      walk(sub, groupKey !== null ? `${groupKey}/${sub.name}` : sub.name, effective)
77	    }
78	  }
79	  walk(tree, null, null)
80	
81	  return result
82	}
